# TurbineH catalogue

> 146 verified components (licence, security scan and contract tests checked) that TurbineH selects
> for apps. Full machine-readable index: https://software.turbineh.com/catalog/index.json · details per component:
> https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/<id> · CLI: `turbineh search "<need>"`.

- [ai.json-repair.jsonrepair](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/ai.json-repair.jsonrepair): Repairs almost-valid JSON produced by models (missing quotes, trailing commas, code fences). Use when: When model output contains non-standard JSON syntax like single quotes or unquoted keys Not when: The component does not validate the shape of the repaired value; use a schema validator afterwards. (use ai.schema-validation.ajv). Provides ai.json-repair.
- [ai.language-detection.franc-min](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/ai.language-detection.franc-min): Detects the language of a text offline (route to the right prompt or model, label documents). Use when: When offline language detection is required for 82 supported languages Not when: Short texts (a few words) are unreliable (use ai.text-chunking.sentence-splitter). Provides ai.language-detection.
- [ai.mcp-server.modelcontextprotocol-sdk](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/ai.mcp-server.modelcontextprotocol-sdk): Exposes the app's own tools and data to AI agents through the Model Context Protocol (server side). Use when: When you need to provide a standardized interface for LLMs to interact with your application's data and tools Not when: When you need an orchestrator rather than a protocol implementation for exposing tools (use ai.orchestrator.turbineh). Provides ai.mcp-server.
- [ai.orchestrator.turbineh](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/ai.orchestrator.turbineh): TurbineH component #001: every AI call of the app is orchestrated — a small open model plans the request, TurbineH orchestration decides the route (which open model), whether it is acceptable and which tool to use, and the chosen open model answers; structured output validated with zod, embeddings for knowledge bases, usage per workspace. Use when: When you need an orchestration layer to decide routes, tools, and acceptability for AI calls Not when: When you need to implement the Model Context Protocol instead of TurbineH orchestration (use ai.mcp-server.modelcontextprotocol-sdk). Provides ai.orchestrator.
- [ai.partial-json.partial-json](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/ai.partial-json.partial-json): Parses incomplete JSON while it is still streaming, to show structured results progressively. Use when: When you need to show structured results progressively before the full stream ends Not when: If you need to repair a fully completed but malformed JSON string rather than parsing a live stream (use ai.json-repair.jsonrepair). Provides ai.partial-json.
- [ai.prompt-templates.mustache](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/ai.prompt-templates.mustache): Logic-less templates for prompts and messages: values are inserted, never executed. Use when: When you need to insert values into a template without allowing logic like if/else or loops Not when: Templates must be written by the app owner, never by end users (use end users writing templates). Provides ai.prompt-templates.
- [ai.schema-validation.ajv](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/ai.schema-validation.ajv): Validates JSON against JSON Schema (structured model output, tool arguments, imported data). Use when: When you need to ensure JSON data conforms to JSON Schema drafts 04/06/07/2019-09/2020-12 or RFC8927 Not when: The component does not repair invalid data (use ai.json-repair.jsonrepair). Provides ai.schema-validation.
- [ai.sse-parsing.eventsource-parser](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/ai.sse-parsing.eventsource-parser): Parses Server-Sent Events streams (streamed model answers, progress events). Use when: When you have raw bytes or chunks from a fetch response and need to extract structured SSE messages Not when: If you require a modern, feature-rich client implementation that manages the connection for you (use eventsource-client). Provides ai.sse-parsing.
- [ai.stopwords.stopword](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/ai.stopwords.stopword): Removes stopwords in many languages for keyword extraction and keyword search. Use when: When you need to strip stopwords from an array of words in one of 62 supported languages Not when: The component does not perform stemming or lemmatisation (use stemming or lemmatisation). Provides ai.stopwords.
- [ai.text-chunking.sentence-splitter](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/ai.text-chunking.sentence-splitter): Splits text into sentences and size-bounded chunks with overlap for retrieval (RAG) and summaries. Use when: When you need to segment text into sentences or chunks based on character limits Not when: Sizes are measured in characters; count tokens with ai.token-count when exact budgets matter (use ai.token-count.gpt-tokenizer). Provides ai.text-chunking.
- [ai.token-count.gpt-tokenizer](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/ai.token-count.gpt-tokenizer): Counts and truncates text by tokens (BPE) to keep prompts and context within a budget. Use when: When you need to keep prompts and context within a specific token budget Not when: If you need to split text by semantic sentences rather than BPE tokens (use ai.text-chunking.sentence-splitter). Provides ai.token-count.
- [ai.vector-store.pgvector](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/ai.vector-store.pgvector): Stores and searches embeddings in Postgres with pgvector (Drizzle and SQL helpers), no extra database. Use when: When using PostgreSQL and want to avoid managing a separate vector database Not when: This component does not compute embeddings; they must be provided by an orchestrator. (use ai.orchestrator.turbineh). Provides ai.vector-store.
- [auth.mfa.otpauth](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/auth.mfa.otpauth): TOTP/HOTP one-time passwords for two-factor authentication. Use when: When you need to generate and validate RFC 4226 and RFC 6238 compliant one-time passwords Not when: When you require full session management or a complete authentication solution rather than just OTP logic (use auth.session.better-auth). Provides auth.mfa.
- [auth.session.better-auth](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/auth.session.better-auth): Email/password and OAuth authentication with database-backed sessions and cookie handling. Use when: When TypeScript-based authentication with database sessions is required Not when: The core package does not implement enterprise SSO (SAML) (use auth.mfa.otpauth). Provides auth.session.
- [authz.organizations.better-auth](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/authz.organizations.better-auth): Organizations (workspaces) with members, roles (owner, admin, member), invitations and an active organization per session. Use when: When you need built-in workspace and role management in a TypeScript application Not when: If you only require role-based access control without organization/workspace structures (use authz.roles.turbineh). Provides authz.organizations.
- [authz.roles.turbineh](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/authz.roles.turbineh): Role policy (owner/admin/member) and requireMember guard used by every page and server action. Use when: When implementing workspace-level access control Not when: Does not implement fine-grained per-record permissions (use authz.organizations.better-auth). Provides authz.roles.
- [commerce.cart.zustand](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/commerce.cart.zustand): Small client state store for carts, wizards and UI state. Use when: Small client state management Not when: Not a database (use a database). Provides commerce.cart.
- [content.frontmatter.gray-matter](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/content.frontmatter.gray-matter): Parses Markdown files with front matter (title, date, tags) for blogs and pages. Use when: When you need to separate structured metadata from a Markdown string or file Not when: If you need to render Markdown to HTML (use content.markdown.react-markdown). Provides content.blog.
- [content.html-dom.linkedom](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/content.html-dom.linkedom): Lightweight server-side DOM to parse and query HTML without a browser. Use when: When you need a lightweight DOM implementation for server-side environments Not when: If you need a different parsing API or specific library ecosystem (use content.html-parse.cheerio). Provides content.html-dom.
- [content.html-parse.cheerio](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/content.html-parse.cheerio): Parses HTML and extracts data with CSS selectors (structured extraction from pages and emails). Use when: When you need to parse HTML and manipulate it using a jQuery-like syntax Not when: If you only need to parse frontmatter instead of full HTML content (use content.frontmatter.gray-matter). Provides content.html-parse.
- [content.html-to-markdown.node-html-markdown](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/content.html-to-markdown.node-html-markdown): Converts HTML to Markdown fast and without a browser DOM (compact context for models, imports). Use when: When you need to convert HTML to Markdown without a browser DOM Not when: If you need a full DOM environment (use content.html-dom.linkedom). Provides content.html-to-markdown.
- [content.markdown-to-text.remove-markdown](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/content.markdown-to-text.remove-markdown): Turns Markdown (e.g. a model answer) into plain text for SMS, notifications or speech. Use when: When you need to strip Markdown formatting to obtain plain text Not when: It is not a sanitizer; you must escape or sanitize before rendering as HTML (use content.html-parse.cheerio). Provides content.markdown-to-text.
- [content.markdown.react-markdown](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/content.markdown.react-markdown): Renders Markdown as React elements without dangerouslySetInnerHTML. Use when: When you need to render markdown safely without using dangerouslySetInnerHTML Not when: If you need to use JavaScript and JSX inside markdown files (use MDX). Provides ui.markdown.
- [content.readability.mozilla-readability](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/content.readability.mozilla-readability): Extracts the main article content of a web page, dropping navigation, ads and boilerplate. Use when: When you have a DOM document and need to isolate the core article text and title Not when: This component requires an existing DOM document and does not fetch pages itself (use content.html-dom.linkedom). Provides content.readability.
- [content.reading-time.reading-time](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/content.reading-time.reading-time): Estimates reading time of an article. Use when: When you need a simple estimation of minutes based on word count Not when: The component does not parse Markdown (use content.markdown.react-markdown). Provides content.blog.
- [content.rss.feed](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/content.rss.feed): Generates RSS 2.0, Atom and JSON feeds for blogs and news. Use when: When you need to create syndication files from existing content data Not when: This component does not fetch or parse feeds; it only generates them. (use content.html-parse.cheerio). Provides content.rss.
- [data.countries.i18n-iso-countries](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/data.countries.i18n-iso-countries): ISO 3166 country codes and localised country names for addresses and shipping. Use when: When you need to display country names in multiple languages based on ISO codes Not when: Does not validate postal addresses (use postal address validation logic). Provides data.countries.
- [data.csv-export.csv-stringify](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/data.csv-export.csv-stringify): Streaming and sync CSV serialisation with quoting. Use when: When you need to convert records to CSV via streaming, callback, or synchronous APIs Not when: If you require different export logic (use data.csv-export.turbineh). Provides data.csv-export.
- [data.csv-export.turbineh](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/data.csv-export.turbineh): CSV export of workspace-scoped records with spreadsheet formula-injection neutralisation. Use when: When you need to export data to CSV while neutralizing potential formula injection attacks Not when: If you require a different CSV generation implementation (use data.csv-export.csv-stringify). Provides data.csv-export.
- [data.csv-import.papaparse](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/data.csv-import.papaparse): Robust CSV parsing with headers, quoting and type detection. Use when: When you need to parse CSV in the browser using web workers to keep the UI reactive Not when: If you require a different implementation for CSV import (use data.csv-import.turbineh). Provides data.csv-import.
- [data.csv-import.turbineh](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/data.csv-import.turbineh): CSV import with size and row limits where every row is validated before insert. Use when: When you need to validate every row before insertion and enforce strict resource limits Not when: When you need to map arbitrary column names or merge duplicates (use data.csv-import.papaparse). Provides data.csv-import.
- [data.dates.date-fns](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/data.dates.date-fns): Pure date arithmetic, comparison and formatting functions. Use when: When performing date calculations or parsing ISO strings Not when: Does not handle time zones by itself (use date-fns-tz). Provides data.dates.
- [data.dates.dayjs](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/data.dates.dayjs): Small immutable date library for parsing, arithmetic and formatting. Use when: When a lightweight (2KB) immutable date library is required Not when: If you require a different functional approach to date manipulation (use data.dates.date-fns). Provides data.dates.
- [data.diff.diff](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/data.diff.diff): Text and line diffs for change history and reviews. Use when: When you need to identify added or removed lines in text blocks Not when: Does not merge conflicting edits (use a merge algorithm). Provides data.diff.
- [data.duration.ms](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/data.duration.ms): Converts human-readable durations to milliseconds and back. Use when: When you need to parse or format simple time durations like '2h' or '1m' Not when: Does not handle calendar months (use data.dates.date-fns). Provides data.dates.
- [data.fetching.react-query](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/data.fetching.react-query): Client data fetching with caching, retries and background refresh. Use when: When you need transport/protocol agnostic data fetching (REST, GraphQL, promises) Not when: The library is designed for managing asynchronous data synchronization rather than simple local state. (use manual state management). Provides data.fetching.
- [data.fuzzy-search.fuse](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/data.fuzzy-search.fuse): Client-side fuzzy search over small collections. Use when: When performing fuzzy searches on small datasets locally Not when: Does not replace database full-text search for large datasets (use database full-text search). Provides data.fuzzy-search.
- [data.ics-export.ical-generator](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/data.ics-export.ical-generator): Generates iCalendar (.ics) feeds and invitations. Use when: When you need to generate a string representation of a calendar containing events Not when: The component does not sync with external calendars (use external calendar synchronization). Provides data.ics-export.
- [data.ids.cuid2](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/data.ids.cuid2): Collision-resistant, unguessable ids. Use when: When you need secure IDs that do not reveal information about the data or the sequence Not when: High performance tight loops like render loops where cross-host uniqueness and security are not required (use a simple counter). Provides data.ids.
- [data.ids.nanoid](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/data.ids.nanoid): Compact, URL-safe, cryptographically strong unique IDs. Use when: When needing cryptographically strong IDs that are smaller than UUIDs Not when: Does not guarantee ordering by creation time (use a sequential integer or timestamp-based approach). Provides data.ids.
- [data.ids.ulid](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/data.ids.ulid): Time-sortable unique ids. Use when: When you need identifiers that are both unique and sortable by time Not when: If you require purely random distribution without time-based sorting or lexicographical order (use UUID v4). Provides data.ids.
- [data.ids.uuid](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/data.ids.uuid): RFC 9562 UUID generation (v4, v7) and validation. Use when: When RFC 9562 compliance is required Not when: Does not shorten ids for URLs (use shortening ids for URLs). Provides data.ids.
- [data.money.currency-js](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/data.money.currency-js): Exact money arithmetic and formatting. Use when: When performing addition or multiplication on monetary values to avoid floating point errors Not when: Does not convert currencies (use currency conversion). Provides data.money.

Use when: When precision is required in terms of significant digits rather than decimal places Not when: The component does not format currencies (use Intl.NumberFormat). Provides data.money.
- [data.money.dinero](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/data.money.dinero): Immutable money objects with currency, allocation and integer minor units. Use when: When you need side-effect free money calculations using integer minor units Not when: Does not fetch exchange rates (use a manual approach). Provides data.money.

Use when: When requiring a lightweight (~7.4kb) tree-shakeable ORM with zero dependencies Not when: Does not provide connection pooling by itself (use manual connection management). Provides data.orm.
- [data.pagination.turbineh](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/data.pagination.turbineh): Offset pagination and bounded free-text search for server-rendered lists. Use when: When implementing server-side pagination with fixed page sizes Not when: Does not provide full-text ranking (use data.fuzzy-search.fuse). Provides data.pagination.

Provides data.phone.
- [data.recurrence.rrule](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/data.recurrence.rrule): RFC 5545 recurrence rules (weekly, monthly...) and occurrence expansion. Use when: When you need to calculate calendar event repetitions (weekly, monthly, etc.) Not when: This component does not store events or send reminders; it only handles recurrence logic. (use data.ics-export.ical-generator). Provides data.recurrence.
- [data.search-index.minisearch](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/data.search-index.minisearch): In-memory full-text search with prefix and fuzzy matching for catalogs and docs. Use when: When data fits locally in process memory Not when: If you need a different fuzzy search implementation (use data.fuzzy-search.fuse). Provides data.search-index.
- [data.serialization.superjson](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/data.serialization.superjson): Serialises Dates, Maps, Sets and BigInts across the network boundary. Use when: When you need to transmit complex JavaScript expressions like Dates or Maps via JSON-compatible interfaces Not when: Superjson is a wrapper for JSON serialization; use standard JSON if you do not need to preserve complex types. (use JSON.stringify). Provides data.serialization.
- [data.slug.slugify](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/data.slug.slugify): Turns titles into URL slugs with transliteration. Use when: When you need to transform strings into lowercase, strict URL slugs Not when: Does not ensure uniqueness against a database (use database uniqueness check). Provides data.slug.
- [data.timezones.date-fns-tz](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/data.timezones.date-fns-tz): Time-zone aware formatting and conversion on top of date-fns. Use when: When using date-fns v3 and needing time zone support without adding large time zone data to bundles Not when: If you prefer a library that provides its own date-time classes instead of working with plain JS Date objects (use data.dates.dayjs). Use when: When small bundle size is required Not when: The documentation suggests Zod as a comparison point for bundle size benefits. (use data.validation.zod). Provides data.validation.

Use when: When you need to coerce input values into specific types via casting Not when: Does not provide compile-time inference as strong as zod (use zod). Provides data.validation.

Use when: When TypeScript-first schema declaration and static type inference are required Not when: Zod does not parse CSV data (use data.csv-import.papaparse). Provides data.validation.
